title: Screens and Online Life
summary: Time online, comparing and feeling judged on social media, sleep and focus, and offline balance.
clinicianNotes: Ask about online safety, including contact from strangers, and follow child-protection procedures. Topic areas are informed by general published work on stress, mood and wellbeing. All items are original wording and are not copied or adapted from any instrument. Bands are provisional and not clinically validated. Use the summary to guide your own questions. Draft content: needs review by a licensed psychologist, and a topic-specific reference list should be added during that review.
prompt: Thinking about the last two weeks, how true is this for you?

domains.label: Time online
domains.description: Using the phone more than intended.

guidance.ok: On time online, things look manageable. Ask what helps, and whether anything has changed recently.
guidance.watch: On time online, some strain is showing. Explore when it began, what triggers it, and what the person already does about it. Ask what the phone gives the teen and what it takes away.
guidance.explore: On time online, the person is strongly affected. Explore how long this has lasted, how it affects daily life, and whether a structured assessment is warranted. Ask what the phone gives the teen and what it takes away.

domains.label: Comparing and feeling judged
domains.description: Feeling worse after social media and pressure to look perfect.

guidance.ok: On comparing and feeling judged, things look manageable. Ask what helps, and whether anything has changed recently.
guidance.watch: On comparing and feeling judged, some strain is showing. Explore when it began, what triggers it, and what the person already does about it. Explore which accounts or apps affect mood most.
guidance.explore: On comparing and feeling judged, the person is strongly affected. Explore how long this has lasted, how it affects daily life, and whether a structured assessment is warranted. Explore which accounts or apps affect mood most.

domains.label: Sleep and focus
domains.description: Late-night phone use affecting rest and homework.

guidance.ok: On sleep and focus, things look manageable. Ask what helps, and whether anything has changed recently.
guidance.watch: On sleep and focus, some strain is showing. Explore when it began, what triggers it, and what the person already does about it. Explore a phone-free wind-down and where the phone sleeps.
guidance.explore: On sleep and focus, the person is strongly affected. Explore how long this has lasted, how it affects daily life, and whether a structured assessment is warranted. Explore a phone-free wind-down and where the phone sleeps.

domains.label: Offline balance
domains.description: Time with people and hobbies away from screens.

guidance.ok: On offline balance, there is a strength to build on. Use it when planning next steps.
guidance.watch: On offline balance, support is partly in place. Explore what helps and what gets in the way. Build on offline activities that already work.
guidance.explore: On offline balance, support looks thin. Explore what is missing, who or what could help, and small first steps. Build on offline activities that already work.

items.text: I stay on my phone longer than I mean to.
I check my phone first thing and last thing every day.
It is hard to put my phone down even when I want to.
I feel worse about myself after looking at social media.
I worry about how many likes or views I get.
I feel pressure to look perfect online.
I use my phone in bed late at night.
Screens make it hard to focus on homework.
I feel tired at school because of late-night scrolling.
I spend time offline with friends or family.
I have hobbies that do not need a screen.
I can switch off notifications when I want to.
